newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha prices stable despite weaker crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha prices stable despite weaker crudes.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices held their ground in slim trading on Wednesday in spite of weaker crude prices, supported by tight physical supplies, market participants said.
Tight prompt availability boosted sentiment for near-term spreads, with second-half April/second-half May assessed at plus $6.50/7.50, 50 cents wider than Tuesday.
First-half May open-spec naphtha was quoted at $228.00/230.00 per tonne. It was assessed at $228.50/229.50 on Tuesday. Bids for second-half May were heard at $225.50 against offers at $226.50.
In late Tuesday dealing, first-half June was sold by a western trader to another western trader at $223.00.
In middle distillates, Japan was expected to have buying interest for two to three spot jet cargoes for April delivery.
April requirements for spot dual purpose kerosene cargoes, which can be used for household heating, have yet to surface in the market, traders said.
Levels for jet kerosene cargoes were notionally assessed at $1.70 to $1.90 over the mean of Singapore quotes on a cost and freight (C and F) basis, they said.
